name: GE Vernova Inc.
blurb: GE Vernova is the power and energy spinoff of General Electric, separated as an independent NYSE-listed company in April 2024. The company operates three segments: Power (gas turbines, steam turbines, grid services), Wind (onshore and offshore turbines), and Electrification (grid software, power conversion, high-voltage equipment). It is one of the few companies in the world capable of manufacturing heavy-duty gas turbines at scale, a competitive moat that has become highly significant as hyperscalers race to secure reliable power for AI data centres.
recent: GE Vernova reported Q1 2026 revenue of $9.34 billion and net income of $4.75 billion, driven by record AI-linked orders. Its total backlog reached $150 billion — described by management as 'sold out for years.' The stock rose from its April 2024 IPO price of approximately $165 to $1,099 as of early May 2026, a gain of roughly 565%, making it one of the best-performing large-cap equities of the AI infrastructure cycle. Gas turbine lead times have stretched into the early 2030s, cementing GEV's pricing power. In 2025 full-year revenue was $38.1 billion (+9%), with net income of $4.9 billion, up 215% year-on-year. Analysts maintain a consensus Buy rating but the average 12-month price target of $1,068 implies the stock has largely priced in near-term upside.
